item.title: Jack Nicholson was scary. But Shelley Duvall delivered the real horror in 'The Shining'
item.description: Just in time for Halloween, NPR correspondent Brian Mann caught 'The Shining' on the big screen — and it changed how he understood the movie.

item.title: After last year's storm, this remote Alaska town is still picking up the pieces
item.description: In October, 2025, the remnants of a typhoon seriously damaged Alaska Native villages in the far western part of the state. A year later, one of the hardest hit communities is still recovering.

item.title: 100 years later, Harry Houdini's death still haunts Detroit
item.description: The legacy of magician Harry Houdini still looms large in Detroit 100 years after his death there. Some mark the anniversary of Houdini's death by trying to make contact with his spirit.

item.title: Judge orders an inquiry into potential DOJ misconduct in Trump's golf course case
item.description: A federal judge is opening an formal inquiry into Trump officials' conduct in the East Potomac case, including whether they misled the court about their plans for the municipal golf course.

item.title: How Esther Perel's parents' experience as Holocaust survivors shaped her worldview

item.title: Kazuo Ishiguro on 'Klara and the Sun' and writing novels about the future
item.description: The Nobel Prize-winning novelist says he honed his skills while working as a songwriter. Now, Ishiguro's 2021 novel Klara and the Sun has been adapted to film. Originally broadcast March 17, 2021.
